text: 0086: approve the plan (9 strands; data shape of the hold record; how a programme close is recorded)
context:
P5 as braid 0086: 9 strands on preset `free` with the PM-run line. The full plan is in the coordinator's message to the PM thread.

Strands: A mockups (the worker stops for the user's look) · C one hold record in `.braid/pauses.json` (ask:data; fixes yd2t) · B limits as what is left (qap7, 7ija) · D lanes collapse and the Held lane, plus a held forwarded question in the Questions panel · E Hold/Go on cards and programmes, sent and counted by code through one seam for 0080 · F Hold all · G finishing a programme, with the Finished and Held/Paused groups · H skills (ask:process, the user merges) · I docs.

Two decisions:
1. Data: the hold record gains optional fields (`waitsFor`, `programme`, who held it), and `by` keeps today's values, because an older `braid` drops a record whose `by` it doesn't know.
2. The close of a programme: recorded as a request on `braid-requests` (the user's Close is the record, with who and when), so only the PM writes `pm/<slug>`. The alternative is the CLI writing `state: done` on the PM's branch.
options: Approve, close as a request record

events.text: A. Approve, with the close as a request record. The hold record's new optional fields with `by` kept in today's values are approved; show the older-reader check in the report. 0086/H's PR comes to me for the user's merge.
events.reason: approve with the close as a request record, because only the PM then writes pm/<slug> and the user's close is on record with who and when, instead of the CLI committing state: done (two writers on one branch)
